info.title: Start Node
info.subtitle: Workflow entry point
info.description: The Start node marks the beginning of every workflow execution. It passes control to the next connected node when the workflow is triggered.
info.triggerDesc: Starts the workflow when triggered manually, via webhook, or on schedule
info.outputDesc: Connects to one node to begin the workflow execution chain
info.requiredDesc: Every workflow must have exactly one Start node
info.immutableDesc: Cannot be deleted or duplicated. Protected workflow entry

overview.title: Start Node Overview
overview.subtitle: The entry point of your workflow execution
overview.description: The Start Node marks the beginning of your workflow. When a workflow is executed, it always begins from this node. You can have only one start node per workflow.

features.title: Features
list: Cannot be deleted or copied (workflow integrity)
Visual indicator for workflow start point

bestPractices.title: Best Practices:
list: Place the start node at the top or left of your workflow
Connect it to your first processing node
Use descriptive names for better workflow readability

limitations.title: Limitations:
list: Only one start node per workflow
Fixed position in some workflow layouts

info.title: End Node
info.subtitle: Workflow termination point
info.description: The End node marks where workflow execution stops. It receives the final output from the previous node and terminates the workflow.
info.inputDesc: Receives the final output from the last node in the workflow
info.terminationDesc: Stops workflow execution when reached. No further nodes execute
info.multipleDesc: You can have multiple End nodes for different workflow branches

info.title: Text Node
info.subtitle: String value storage
info.description: The Text node holds a string value that can be manually entered or received from another node, and passed forward in the workflow.
info.manualInput: Enter text manually or receive value from a connected node
info.inputHandle: Input handle receives string data from API, LLM, or other nodes
info.outputHandle: Output handle sends the text value to downstream nodes

input-text.label: Input Text
input-text.description: The string value to be converted

info.title: Uppercase Node
info.subtitle: Text case modifier
info.description: The Uppercase node processes string text values and converts all alphabetic characters to uppercase format. It can process text entered manually or received from preceding nodes.
info.rule1: Accepts any text inputs via target handle or direct manual input.
info.rule2: Outputs the converted uppercase string to downstream target nodes.
info.rule3: Non-alphabetic characters (numbers, punctuation, emojis) are left unchanged.

outputNode.label: Output
outputNode.description: Visualizes output data in different formats

output-data.label: Input Data
output-data.description: Raw data passed to Output Node

info.title: Output Node
info.subtitle: Data Visualization & Preview
info.description: The Output node acts as a viewer endpoint in your workflow. It receives processed data from preceding nodes and displays it in a format of your choice, such as plain text, PDF, images, raw source code, or JSON structures.
info.rule1: Accepts exactly one input connection via its left target handle.
info.rule2: Select a display format from the dropdown to format the raw input data accordingly.
info.rule3: Supports previewing live outputs like images, formatted code snippets, or raw JSON structures.
